candidates.title: PRT bridge preflights every job at the current tip's block context (block.number = tip), so an honest timeout win or inner-tournament win whose window opens at block `first` reverts at tip first-1 and lands at least one block late; in a one-block window it is never sent
candidates.component: PRT bridge and transaction journal in doc/recipes (prt-transactions.lua methods:submit; prt-bridge.lua methods:tick/attempt/jobs)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support'); stands in for the honest operator's 'Submitting transactions'
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:submit: line 161-163 (block = latest, nonce at block.hash), line 173 (window check against tip + 1), line 218 (chain:simulate at {blockHash = block.hash}), lines 223-226 (eth_estimateGas at block.number); doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:jobs lines 403-405 (winMatchByTimeout first = responderDeadline / min(d1,d2)), 418-423 (winInnerTournament first = resultAt), methods:tick line 714/749 (due when tip + 1 >= first), lines 770-771 (a rejected preflight returns 'published' = true), line 781 (wakes at tip = first - 1 to attempt), methods:attempt lines 671-674 (self.rejected[job.key] = tip_hash). Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7: Clock.deadline/remainingAt and MatchClocks.classifyTimeoutAt (a responder is expired at current == deadline), Tournament._isClosed/_resultAt/innerResult (block.number from Time.currentTime).
candidates.description: The bridge treats a job as due when the NEXT block can include it (tip + 1 >= first), and it wakes at tip = first - 1 for exactly that purpose. But the journal's preflight (eth_call at the latest block's hash) and gas estimate (eth_estimateGas at latest block.number) execute with block.number = tip, not tip + 1 (anvil and geth both use the requested block's header; verified on anvil 1.5.1: eth_call of NUMBER at the tip's hash returns the tip, 'pending' returns tip + 1). Every honest action whose validity STARTS at a block, i.e. winMatchByTimeout (valid from the opponent's responderDeadline, or from min(d1,d2) in a sealed leaf race) and winInnerTournament (valid from the child's resultAt when the child closes after its last deletion), is therefore not yet valid in the preflight at tip = first - 1: it reverts with code 3, the bridge records self.rejected[job.key] = tip_hash, prints 'preflight reverted', and retries only at tip = first, so the transaction can land at first + 1 at the earliest. One block of the window is lost on every such action. When the honest win's window is one block long ([D, D+1): winner allowance of one block, or a leaf race where the honest clock exceeds the other by one block), the action is never published: at tip D its window check (tip + 1 >= last) already fails, and the match becomes eliminable, removing the honest claim. In addition, the rejection is reported to crisium as 'published', so crisium passes again at the same tip; tick then skips the rejected win and publishes the next due job (a permissionless cleanup or a bond recovery) at the free nonce, and at the next tip the R1-A8-4 pending-job preference keeps the win behind that transaction for a whole inclusion. The same off-by-one also delays every cleanup with a start block (eliminateMatchByTimeout, eliminateInnerTournament, stageTournamentResult, tryRecoveringBond, acceptStagedTournamentResult), which is harmless by itself.
candidates.trigger: Any adversary that stops answering a match against the honest claim (section 7: 'Post any number of claims (Sybils) ... and abandon or defend them at will'), or a child tournament that the honest claim wins alone and that closes after its last deletion. No special timing is needed for the one-block loss: it is deterministic on every timeout or inner win. A tight window arises when the honest winner's paused allowance is small (the same margin state as in R1-A8-4: after absorbed censorship/inclusion delays), or in a leaf race whose clocks differ by one block, which the adversary arranges by spending its own clock. The cleanup fall-through additionally needs any due open-ended job at that tip (adversary Sybil match eliminable, or the honest's own bond recovery).
candidates.reachability: Reached with the recipe as written and default options (cleanup on): the bridge's own next_block computation wakes it at tip = first - 1, and the observation of the match event is many blocks old by then, so the rejection happens at every start-window action. The preflight block context is a property of eth_call/eth_estimateGas on the supported nodes (anvil, geth), checked on anvil in the scratch directory. A one-block window is reachable: Dave's win is valid in [D, D + A) for a paused winner with allowance A (MatchClocks._classifySoleSurvivorAt requires remaining > overdue), and A can be any positive value the honest claim's clock holds at that moment.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No. The trigger is an abandoned match or a child the honest claim wins, ordinary capabilities of section 7; it needs no machine-API access by an untrusted party, no unguaranteed directory, no reorg beyond the input policy, no violation of A1-A8 by the deployment (Dave's clocks follow their documented inclusive-expiry rule, the bridge mis-times against it), and it is not an application stall.

2. Role: Support. AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes, the cartesi-machine CLI, ... | Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.' Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator ... Any other support defect is Low.' The bridge and journal stand in for the honest operator's path item 'Submitting transactions'. No honest-operator component of the AUDIT.md table (interpreter, hash tree, log producers, delivery, store/load) shows the defect.
3. High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium.' This applies if the stood-in rating (step 4) is High or Critical.

4. Critical in the stood-in honest-operator role: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' and section 1 'Completeness failure. The honest operator ... cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.' At a reachable state (honest winner with a one-block window, or with less margin left than its inclusion time plus one block) the honest win is sent too late or never, although the chain would include it in the next block; section 8: 'violating any rule or obligation at a reachable state, or anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical'. Stood-in Critical, so Medium as support. Second reading: if the goal's 'the chain includes its transactions within the dispute clocks' is read to absorb a one-block self-inflicted delay per action (Dave charges a win only beyond one responseBudget), the stood-in defect is only a constant erosion of the inclusion budget (High as 'multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor' does not fit well; Low otherwise). The fact that decides: whether a window of fewer blocks than the honest inclusion time plus one is a state the clocks must still let the honest claim win, which Dave's design (win valid while remaining > overdue) says it is.
5. Not needed (Medium under the preferred reading).
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for a Critical R4 completeness failure in the honest-operator role); Low under the reading that one block per action is inclusion slack the clocks absorb
candidates.threat_to_goal: In an operator built on the recipe, every timeout or inner-tournament win of the honest claim is one block late and, at a one-block margin, not sent at all, so the honest claim is eliminated by eliminateMatchByTimeout/eliminateInnerTournament and a dishonest claim can settle its state (completeness failure of section 1). The rejection also feeds the R1-A8-4 cleanup preference, adding a full inclusion of delay with no prior pending cleanup needed.

candidates.test_idea: Copy the scratch test into bugs/<ID>/test.lua: one match where the honest claim is commitment two and the opponent's responderDeadline is D; mock chain evaluates eth_call/eth_estimateGas at the given block's number and includes a nonce's newest candidate in the next block. Assert that the honest winMatchByTimeout lands in block D (published at tip D-1) for windows [D, D+6) and [D, D+1). A fix (preflight with a block override of number + 1, or the 'pending' tag with the account's own pending candidate excluded, or not marking the job rejected when the revert is only 'not yet valid' and the window opens at tip + 1) makes it pass; bugs/R1-A8-4 and prt-bridge-test.lua must still pass.

candidates.title: PRT transaction journal cannot re-price a pending honest move once its priority fee reached --max-priority-fee: fees() rejects the bumped priority, so the candidate is frozen at its signing-time max fee (blocked 'fee_ceiling') while --max-fee still has room and the base fee rises above it
candidates.component: PRT transaction journal in doc/recipes (prt-transactions.lua methods:fees and methods:submit), used by prt-bridge.lua
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support'); stands in for the honest operator's 'Submitting transactions'
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:fees lines 140-154 (priority = min(max(suggested, min), max_priority); with a previous candidate priority = max(priority, ceil(prev.priority * 1.15)); returns nil when priority > max_priority); methods:submit lines 192-211 (no fee -> outbid only a dropped candidate -> otherwise { blocked = 'fee_ceiling' }); defaults lines 306-310 (bump 15%, min priority 1 gwei, max priority 10 gwei, max fee 100 gwei); prt-bridge.lua methods:tick/attempt/report_blocked (the blocked result only reports an anomaly; the same frozen nonce also blocks R1-A8-4-style replacements and cancels).
candidates.description: A same-nonce replacement must raise both the max fee and the priority fee by bump_percent (and nodes require it). fees() computes the replacement priority as at least 115% of the previous one and refuses the replacement whenever that exceeds max_priority_fee, even when the max fee needed for inclusion is well below --max-fee. The first candidate is signed with priority = min(eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas suggestion, max_priority_fee) and max fee = min(2 * base + priority, max_fee). So once a candidate carries the priority cap (immediately when the node suggests >= 10 gwei, or after about 17 bumps from 1 gwei since every bump raises the priority by 15% whether or not the tip is the problem), no later submit at that nonce can be signed: the journal returns blocked = 'fee_ceiling'. The candidate stays at its signing-time max fee. If the base fee then rises above that max fee, the honest move cannot be included and cannot be re-priced, although --max-fee leaves room (in the test: max fee 30 gwei frozen while the base fee is 40 gwei and --max-fee is 100 gwei). The frozen nonce also blocks replacing that candidate with another job (the obsolete/cancel path), so every later honest move waits until the base fee falls below the frozen max fee.
candidates.trigger: An adversary raises activity on the chain (section 7: 'Raise activity on the chain that does not belong to the application ...'; 'Race and reorder transactions within the chain's rules'): it fills blocks so that the base fee rises 12.5% per block past the honest candidate's max fee (about 6 full blocks double it), and keeps blocks at or above the target to hold it there. The priority cap is reached either because the node's tip suggestion is at least 10/1.15 = 8.7 gwei (congestion, or recent blocks whose cheapest transactions tip high) or after the bridge's own repeated bumps of a stuck candidate. The adversary then only has to hold the base fee above the frozen max fee (e.g. 30 gwei), instead of above the configured --max-fee (100 gwei) that the honest operator is willing to pay.
candidates.reachability: Reached with the default options. The test reproduces it with the real journal: suggestion 10 gwei, base 10 gwei -> candidate max fee 30 gwei, priority 10 gwei; three blocks later, base 40 gwei: submit returns blocked = 'fee_ceiling'. No machine state is involved; any honest deadline move (advanceMatch, seal, leaf proof, timeout win, join) can be the frozen candidate.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Arguably not: the trigger is chain activity that section 7 grants the adversary, not a deep reorg, a host fault or an API misuse. A reading that treats any fee-market condition as part of 'the chain includes its transactions within the dispute clocks' would put it outside the goal's assumption; but the defect is that the honest operator refuses to re-price within its own configured budget, which the chain assumption does not excuse.

2. Role: Support. AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.' Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator.' The journal stands in for 'Submitting transactions'.
3. High/Medium cases: 'A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium', if step 4 gives High or Critical in the stood-in role.

4. Stood-in honest operator: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' At a reachable state (pending honest move at the priority cap, base fee above its max fee but below --max-fee) the operator stops re-pricing and its deadline move is not included until the window closes, so the honest claim can lose by timeout (section 1 completeness failure). Critical in that role, hence Medium as support. Alternative: if the clocks' censorship budget is read to cover any fee-driven non-inclusion, this is only a cheaper way to achieve such a delay (constant-factor reduction of the adversary's cost), Low.
5. Not needed under the preferred reading.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for a Critical R4 violation) / Low (if fee-market non-inclusion is read as part of the chain-inclusion assumption)
candidates.threat_to_goal: An operator built on the journal can be held out of the chain at a base fee far below what it is configured to pay, so its responses miss the dispute clocks and the honest claim is eliminated by timeout; the frozen nonce also stalls every later honest move of every epoch.
candidates.evidence: Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSCHED/test-fees.lua drives the real prt-transactions.lua journal (defaults) over a mock chain. Output on audit/prt2 (exit 1): 'tip 10: base 10 gwei, suggested tip 10 gwei: signed max fee 30000000000, priority 10000000000' then 'tip 13: base 40 gwei (candidate unincludable, --max-fee 100 gwei): not re-priced: fee_ceiling'.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua as the scratch test: first submit with eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas = 10 gwei and base 10 gwei; advance bump_blocks blocks with base 40 gwei and the nonce unmined; assert that submit publishes a replacement whose max fee covers base + priority (it passes if fees() allows the replacement priority to exceed max_priority_fee for re-pricing, or signs initial candidates below the cap leaving bump room, e.g. priority <= max_priority / 1.15^k).

not_covered: Gas-limit sufficiency of 2x eth_estimateGas when the adversary adds a dangling commitment between estimate and inclusion (pairing branch): reasoned from Dave's Gas.sol allocations (WIN_MATCH_BY_TIMEOUT 236k incl. dangling re-pairing) and storage writes that 2x covers it; not measured with forge or the chain harness (did not want to recompile the shared Dave tree).
EIP-7825 per-transaction cap vs. the out-of-gas retry (2 x exhausted gas can exceed 2^24 for winLeafMatch): no reachable out-of-gas found, so not pursued.

Cross-epoch branch of methods:tick ('Another epoch's pending transaction is left alone until it is mined'), the variant R1-A8-4 itself points at: checked reachability and found that an older epoch's open-ended jobs (bond recoveries, acceptance) are finished before the next epoch's honest deadline moves exist in normal operation (only one live dispute, next seal at acceptance); not reported, but the R1-A8-4 fix does not cover that branch.

crisium idle() iterates listeners newest first, i.e. the open epoch's input before the sealed epoch's agreed-pair step, contrary to its comment ('sealed epochs first'); it only reorders work inside one non-preemptive idle step (R1-A7-3), so not reported.

Epoch seal observed only under the input policy (finalized by default) while the dispute uses depth 4: the root join waits for finality and the late-join deduction charges it to the honest root clock; the threat model requires acting on final history, so this is an A7 sizing question, not analysed.

Observation lag (dispute policy 4 blocks) before each honest response and the receipt-based suppression of a resend for 4 blocks after a reverted honest transaction: design consequence of the policy, not quantified against the clocks.
Base-fee spikes above --max-fee itself and eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas manipulation beyond the frozen-priority case (operator configuration).

No run on the real chain harness (anvil + Dave) of the bridge timing; evidence uses mock chains with semantics checked on anvil only. geth behaviour inferred from its DoCall/DoEstimateGas using the requested header, not run.
prt.lua player work scheduling beyond idle/epoch_sealed/agreed pair (bundle opening and proof preparation latency are R12 costs covered by earlier candidates).
Sentinel mode (watch) timing and anomaly reporting; Arbitrum/L2 block-number semantics.
